Jesse to share pricing tiers and reserved capacity options
Maya to prepare benchmark plan and sample script for their workloads
Schedule POC kickoff for 2026-05-04 at 10:00 PT

summary: Redwood AE+SE did a console walkthrough for Evergreen Finance focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. Customer is evaluating cost and latency tradeoffs for a mixed hosted + dedicated deployment; security and KMS were key concerns. Agreed next steps: share security pack, run benchmarks, and propose reserved capacity pricing for a pilot.
transcript:
[00:00] Jesse Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're gonna get started in a minute. Uh, quick round of intros?
[00:08] Liam Rodriguez: Liam, CTO, Evergreen Finance. We've got Priya, Daniel, Sara here.
[00:12] Priya Shah: Hi, Priya, head of platform.
[00:14] Daniel Wu: Daniel, infra, hi.
[00:16] Sara Lopez: Sara, product.
[00:18] Jesse Park: Great, thanks. I'm Jesse, AE at Redwood. Maya is our solutions engineer, she'll do most of the console demo.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Hi all. Quick agenda: show usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown. We'll also touch on routing and dedicated capacity. Please interrupt.
[00:36] Sara Lopez: Sounds good. Our primary goal today is to understand cost and how to attribute spend by feature.
[00:41] Jesse Park: Perfect, that's exactly what the per-route dashboards are for.
[01:05] [01:05] Maya Chen: Alright I'm sharing my screen — bear with me, I have the console up. At the top left you can see organization and project selector, I switched to Evergreen Finance sandbox project.
[01:18] Maya Chen: First tab: usage analytics. By default we show token volume over time, requests per minute, and 95th/99th latency bands. Here you can change date ranges and sampling.
[01:32] Priya Shah: That latency chart looks spiky — is that from batching or from a few long requests?
[01:40] Maya Chen: Good question. We surface a latency breakdown by route — so you can click into routes to see source of spikes. In this tenant we can also filter by model variant and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).
[01:52] [01:52] Maya Chen: Clicking into /api/v1/chat/assistant — this is your chat route — shows per-minute token usage and per-call token distribution. You can see most calls are small (under 150 tokens) with a long tail.
[02:08] Daniel Wu: That's actually similar to our distribution. Can we map that to estimated cost?
[02:12] Maya Chen: Yep — next panel is cost estimation. We model per-token cost using your selected pricing tier; we also break down cost by route, by model, and by time window.
[02:22] Maya Chen: For example, in the last 30 days this route accounts for ~42% of token spend but only 18% of requests.
[02:30] Liam Rodriguez: Is caching included in this calc? We have heavy re-asks where prefix caching could help.
[02:35] Maya Chen: We include caching savings when you enable prefix/KV cache on the serving config. If caching's on we show both gross and net token counts.
[02:44] [02:44] Maya Chen: Another useful view is per-route efficiency — tokens per semantic output. You can surface anomalous prompts that cause token blowups.
[02:55] Sara Lopez: Can we export these per-route reports? Our finance team wants CSVs.
[02:59] Maya Chen: Absolutely, export CSV or scheduled reports via email or webhook.
[03:07] [03:07] Jesse Park: For cost planning a lot of customers like to run a what-if with reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go — show that?
[03:14] Maya Chen: Yep — switching to cost models. Here you can simulate different profiles: hosted API pricing, reserved Dedicated baseline, and a hybrid where the tail goes to Hosted. You can enter commit sizes, expected throughput, and autoscale/burst settings.
[03:28] [03:28] Maya Chen: Notice the cost per 1M tokens goes down when you reserve capacity, but there's an up-front commitment. We also show break-even time given your token growth.
[03:40] Priya Shah: For our throughput — we see monthly 99th of 300ms is important. Does dedicated guarantee latency?
[03:48] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and latency under our SLA, yes. We also provide per-route latency SLOs using routing policies (you can pin critical routes to dedicated pools).
[03:58] Daniel Wu: How does routing handle fallbacks? If dedicated is saturated do we auto-failover to hosted?
[04:04] Maya Chen: Yes — smart routing supports tiered fallbacks. You can configure policies: prefer dedicated, fallback to hosted with model mapping. We also log fallbacks in the console so you can see incidents.
[04:14] [04:14] Maya Chen: Quick note on observability — each request has a trace id; you can jump from a token spike to the raw request, prompt, and response object in the troubleshooting tab.
[04:26] Sara Lopez: We need audit logs for compliance — who accessed what, when?
[04:30] Jesse Park: We have audit logs and you can forward them to your SIEM; plus SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC.
[04:38] Maya Chen: And for encryption — we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured to integrate with cloud KMS.
[04:47] Liam Rodriguez: That matters for us — we need key rotation policies and a network diagram.
[04:52] Jesse Park: We'll include the security pack with diagrams and KMS detail in the follow up.
[04:56] [05:00] Maya Chen: Back to the console — here's the per-route dashboard. You can create custom routes and tag them with business attributes: product, env, owner. Then the cost is roll-up by tag.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Example: tag 'recon' is a high-cost embedding job; you can isolate and throttle it or assign it to cheaper quantized models.
[05:25] Daniel Wu: Do you recommend quantization for embeddings? We worry about quality loss.
[05:29] Maya Chen: For many retrieval workloads 8-bit or 4-bit quantization is acceptable and saves cost. We provide model/quantization recommendations by workload and automated quality monitoring to detect regressions.
[05:41] [05:41] Maya Chen: Let's look at a cost anomaly we detected last week — you can see a spike at 02:14 UTC where a mis-specified prompt caused 10x token usage. The console surfaced an alert and flagged affected routes.
[05:55] Sara Lopez: That's helpful; can alerts tie back to our incident management? PagerDuty?
[05:59] Maya Chen: Yes, we have webhook integrations for PagerDuty, Slack, and email.
[06:05] [06:05] Priya Shah: For the POC — we want to measure both latency and cost sensitivity. Can you run a benchmark that mirrors our mix: chat (70%), embeddings (20%), rerank (10%)?
[06:15] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll need a representative prompt set and sample traffic pattern — we'll run it in both hosted and a small dedicated pool and return per-route cost and latency.
[06:25] Liam Rodriguez: How long do you need to run that? Two weeks?
[06:28] Maya Chen: Typically 3–7 days is fine to get stable numbers, longer if you want seasonality. For reserved capacity sizing we usually look at 30 days of baseline.
[06:40] [06:40] Jesse Park: Quick note on pricing, our hosted tiers are per-token with volume discounts; dedicated is a committed pool with different unit economics. I'll send a spreadsheet with examples.
[06:48] Liam Rodriguez: Please include examples with their actual token distribution — that helps.
[06:52] Jesse Park: Yes — we'll run their token profile through the modeler.
[06:56] [07:00] Maya Chen: Switching to the per-route cost drilldown — each bar is clickable. Here we selected the 'mobile-assist' route: breakdown by model (redwood-3b-quant, redwood-7b, open-source-13b), time window, and request size.
[07:14] Maya Chen: You can also compare two time windows to see if a new prompt rollout increased cost.
[07:20] Sara Lopez: Is there programmatic access? Our pipeline wants per-route cost metrics into our BI tool.
[07:25] Maya Chen: Yes, we expose a metrics API and a Prometheus endpoint for cost and latency metrics. You can also pull CSVs on a schedule.
[07:33] [07:33] Daniel Wu: On the metrics API — what auth? API keys or mTLS?
[07:36] Maya Chen: API keys for programmatic access, and we support mTLS for Private/On-prem. You can also integrate with your IAM via SAML/SCIM for user provisioning.
[07:46] [07:46] Maya Chen: Now a short demo of anomaly detection — we have built-in heuristics and model-based baselining; we detected a pattern that looked like prompt leakage, and you can configure auto-runs of remediation scripts.
[07:58] Liam Rodriguez: Remediation scripts? Like auto-throttle?
[08:00] Maya Chen: Exactly — you can auto-throttle routes, or change model mapping to a cheaper model if cost exceeds threshold.
[08:07] Sara Lopez: Hmm, that's interesting. Could be handy for bursts.
[08:12] [08:12] Maya Chen: I'll show the policy editor — it's a YAML-like UI but with visual toggles. Here a policy pins route X to dedicated, with fallback to hosted-quantized and a throttle after 95th percentile.
[08:27] Priya Shah: For compliance we need an audit trail of policy changes. Is that recorded?
[08:31] Maya Chen: Yes, policy changes are auditable and included in the audit logs.
[08:36] [08:36] Jesse Park: Quick question — any concerns on your side about model compatibility across hosted and dedicated? Some teams worry about small differences in tokenizer or kernel changes.
[08:45] Liam Rodriguez: Yes we want consistent outputs as much as possible.
[08:48] Maya Chen: We maintain model variants and version pinning; there can be differences if you use different quantization or mixed kernels, but the console surfaces similarity metrics and we run diff tests as part of rollouts.
[09:00] [09:00] Daniel Wu: Speaking of rollouts — can we do canary for a subset of users?
[09:03] Maya Chen: Yes, canary rollouts and A/B tests are supported; you can target by header, cookie, or user segment.
[09:12] Sara Lopez: Okay, let's talk PII — any retention concerns? Some of our inputs contain personal data.
[09:17] Jesse Park: We have data retention controls and you can opt-out of storing prompts, use ephemeral KV cache, and we have strict access controls. We'll include details in the security docs.
[09:28] [09:28] Maya Chen: Also note Private deployment keeps data in your VPC; Dedicated isolates compute but still uses Redwood control plane unless you choose Private.
[09:36] Priya Shah: For us, a hybrid looks likely: hosted for low-criticality features, dedicated for high-SLA routes.
[09:43] Maya Chen: That's a common pattern. Now I'm going to show the billing and chargeback view — here you can configure chargeback by tag and set internal rates.
[09:55] Maya Chen: You can also create budgets and alert owners when their tag crosses threshold.
[10:02] [10:02] Liam Rodriguez: Can we backfill cost attribution for last 6 months? Our finance wants historicals.
[10:06] Maya Chen: Yes, if you ingest historical logs we can backfill; otherwise we begin attribution from when tagging is enabled. We usually do a short reconciliation project.
[10:16] [10:16] Maya Chen: One more bit — Optimize recommendations. This tab suggests batching sizes, cache TTLs, and model/quant recommendations based on your observed patterns. It's prescriptive and you can apply suggestions one-click to a route sandbox.
[10:30] Sara Lopez: Do recommendations include expected cost savings?
[10:33] Maya Chen: Yes, each recommendation shows projected savings and impact on latency and accuracy risk (low/medium/high).
[10:42] [10:42] Jesse Park: Alright, let's talk next steps. We'll run a short benchmark with your sample traffic pattern and return per-route cost and latency in 3–7 days. We'll also send the security pack and pricing.
[10:54] Liam Rodriguez: Great — can you include both hosted-only and small dedicated pool numbers?
[10:58] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll do hosted, dedicated small pool, and hybrid.
[11:03] Priya Shah: One ask — please include exact tokenization details so our evaluation team can match tokens.
[11:08] Maya Chen: We'll include tokenizer samples and the benchmark script.
[11:12] [11:12] Jesse Park: Any other questions?
[11:15] Daniel Wu: One quick one — network egress: do you have recommendations to minimize cross-region costs?
[11:20] Maya Chen: Put dedicated pools in the same region as your services; use regional routing policies. We can also advise on VPC peering options in the security doc.
[11:30] Sara Lopez: Okay thanks — that was thorough.
[11:33] Jesse Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and scheduling the POC kickoff.
[11:38] Liam Rodriguez: Thanks, talk soon.
[44:30] [44:30] End of meeting — recording stopped.
